newsitem.title: UK: Sterling debt and futures closing report.
newsitem.headline: Sterling debt and futures closing report.

text.p: Gilts shot higher on Tuesday, as did most major bond markets, closing nearly a point higher and itching to go further as long as Wednesday's raft of data do not prove disruptive. The June gilt future settled 29/32 higher at 109-24 but with Bund and U.S. Treasury bond futures up almost a point apiece that did not represent outperformance. The gilt/Bund spread held steady at around 185/186 basis points. "The gilt will probably go through 109-31 and then maybe reach 110-12 depending on the figures tomorrow," said a senior salesman at a UK brokerage.
"But up there, I would be seriously thinking about switching shorter," he added.

Wednesday sees the release of unemployment, average earnings and PSBR data. A Reuter poll forecasts another sharp drop in unemployment -- 45,000 -- in March with annual average earnings growth expected to slip back to 4.75 percent in February, from 5.0 the month before.
"The rise in average earnings in January may have been exaggerated by bonus payments in the financial services sector," said David Mackie, UK economist at JP Morgan.
"Nevertheless, the upward trend in earnings growth has been in evidence for the last 18 months since service sector firms reported difficulty in recruiting appropriate skilled labour."
Despite a number of distortions to the unemployment data, Philip Shaw, chief UK economist at Union Plc, said the pace of jobless falls had definitely accelerated.

PSBR data for March are forecast to show a shortfall of 9.3 billion pounds. That would leave Britain with a public sector deficit of about 24 billion pounds for the 1996/97 financial year -- well below the government's 26.4 billion forecast but less than impressive for an economy growing at a steady lick.

"It's all very well saying we're heading towards balance -- we should be after five years in a steady recovery," said Jonathan Loynes, UK economist at HSBC Markets. "The problem is what happens if the economy starts to slowdown?"
The gilts salesman said the market had first picked up after Monday's UK producer price data, which showed output prices up only 1.0 percent in the year to March.

A modest 0.1 percent rise in U.S. consumer prices, unveiled at 1230 GMT, then helped the market along. "But the icing on the cake is that the next auction is only two billion stg. That almost creates a shortage of stock," the salesman said.

The Bank of England announced it would sell two billion pounds of 7.0 percent gilts due 2002 on April 23. The salesman said many in the market expected 2.5 or 3.0 billion stg of stock to be sold as the Bank tried to frontload its funding schedule.
The June short sterling future settled three basis points higher at 93.43. Just a week ago, it stood at 93.25, implying at least a half-point rise in base rates by the end of June.
But with inflationary pressures apparently still subdued, those expectations have been scaled back. Now the contract, is not even fully discounting a 50 basis point rate rise.
